title: Polpette al Sugo
subtitle: Italian meatballs in tomato sauce
excerpt: Pork and beef meatballs, herb-seasoned and fried, then simmered in a simple tomato sauce until tender. Serve with pasta, on bruschetta, or with plenty of bread.

recipe.sourceNotes: Polpette al sugo is a staple of Italian family cooking across all regions. Italian-American meatballs in marinara have their roots in this dish, though the Italian original tends to be smaller and less densely spiced.

recipeTools.notes: For frying the meatballs before simmering.

content.text: Polpette al sugo are Italian meatballs made from a mix of pork and beef with breadcrumbs, egg, and herbs, fried until golden, then simmered in a simple tomato sauce. The frying step sets the exterior and adds flavour to the sauce base. The meatballs finish cooking gently in the tomato, which keeps them tender rather than rubbery.

Combine the pork, beef, breadcrumbs, egg, parmesan, garlic, parsley, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Mix well with your hands, then roll into balls about the size of a large marble, around 3 cm across. You should get about 24.

Heat 3 tablespoons of olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the meatballs in batches, turning to brown all over, about 5 minutes per batch. They don't need to be cooked through. Lift out and set aside.

In a large saucepan, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute until pale gold. Add the tinned tomatoes, tomato puree, basil, salt, and sugar. Stir and simmer for 10 minutes.

Add the meatballs to the tomato sauce. Simmer gently, partially covered, for 25 minutes until the meatballs are cooked through and the sauce has thickened. Stir occasionally and add a splash of water if it gets too thick. Taste for salt before serving.
